title: kubernetes: wildcard queries are no longer answered

detection.reason: whether any client issues wildcard queries is request-time behaviour

quote: Wildcard queries are no longer supported by the _kubernetes_ plugin.
remediation: Clients resolving `*.<ns>.svc` / `any.<ns>.svc` names get NXDOMAIN from 1.9.0. Run 1.8.7 first and grep its logs for the deprecation warning to find them.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/coredns --tail=5000 2>/dev/null | grep -ci wildcard  # non-zero on CoreDNS 1.8.7+ = clients are still issuing wildcard queries that 1.9.0 stops answering; 0 proves nothing on older versions, which log no warning

title: route53: plaintext AWS credentials in the Corefile are deprecated

detection.reason: read from the option KEY names the agent extracts inside each Corefile plugin block of every kube-system ConfigMap whose name contains coredns (agent 0.4.58+; older agents leave this NOT_DETECTABLE) — keys only, never values; import lines are not followed — the key NAME only is ever collected

quote: plugin/route53: deprecate plaintext secret in Corefile for route53 plugin
remediation: Move the credentials out of the Corefile: use an IAM role (IRSA / instance profile) or the standard AWS environment/shared-config; the `aws_access_key` option is deprecated and will be removed.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | select(any((.data // {})[]; test("^\\s*aws_access_key\\b"))) | .metadata.name'  # each ConfigMap printed still embeds AWS credentials in its Corefile (values deliberately not printed)

title: template: SERVFAIL when the zone matches but no regex does

detection.reason: template regexes are option values, which are never collected

quote: plugin/template: return SERVFAIL for zone-match regex-no-match case
remediation: Names inside a template's zone that matched none of its `match` regexes used to fall through silently; from 1.9.3 they get SERVFAIL unless `fallthrough` is set. Add `fallthrough` where the next plugin was meant to answer.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*template\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed template block SERVFAILs unmatched names unless fallthrough is set

title: coredns_forward_sockets_open is removed

detection.reason: Prometheus rules and dashboards are not collected

remediation: Drop the series from dashboards and alerts.
verifyCommand: kubectl get prometheusrules -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec | tostring | test("coredns_forward_sockets_open")) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # rules printed reference a series removed in 1.9.4

title: forward: health checks honour force_tcp

detection.reason: read from the option KEY names the agent extracts inside each Corefile plugin block of every kube-system ConfigMap whose name contains coredns (agent 0.4.58+; older agents leave this NOT_DETECTABLE) — keys only, never values; import lines are not followed

remediation: With `force_tcp` set, upstream health probes switch from UDP to TCP at 1.9.0. An upstream that answers UDP but blocks TCP/53 is marked unhealthy and dropped from rotation after the upgrade — check TCP reachability to every upstream first.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*force_tcp\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed forward block now health-checks its upstreams over TCP
